chunks: We said: That which one can be certain of to be the reason for the occultation of the Imam is his fear for his life by murder, due to the oppressors threatening him and preventing him from administering the affairs he is responsible to direct and manage.
If he is prevented from achieving his objective, the duty of assuming the Imamate falls away.

And if he fears for his life, his occultation becomes obligatory and his hiding becomes necessary, just as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) once hid in the valley and another time in the cave, and there is no reason for this except the fear of harm reaching him.

And no one can say that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) only hid from his people after he had delivered what was obligatory for him to deliver and they no longer had any need of him, whereas your statement regarding the Imam is contrary to that.
Furthermore, the hiding of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was not prolonged nor did it last long, whereas the hiding of the Imam has seen ages pass and eras vanish.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological justification for the Imam's occultation based on fear and protection?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi grounds the necessity of the Imam's occultation (ghayba) in the principle of *khawf* (fear of death) from oppressive rulers, framing it as a divine preservation strategy rather than a failure of duty. He draws a parallel to the Prophet Muhammad’s temporary concealment in the valley and cave, while distinguishing the Imam's prolonged, centuries-long occultation as a unique phase of leadership necessitated by the specific political climate. This argument reinforces the Shia view that the Imam remains the valid authority even when physically hidden from public view.
